title: Unpivot Course Completion Data by Quarter
prompt: You manage an online course platform that tracks quarterly completion counts for each course. The `course_completions` table stores data in wide format: one row per course with separate columns for each quarter's completion count (q1_completions, q2_completions, q3_completions, q4_completions). Your analytics team needs this data in long format where each row represents one course-quarter pair. Transform the data into three columns: `course_id`, `quarter` (with values 'Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'), and `completion_count`. Include rows where the completion count is NULL (some courses may not have data for all quarters). Order the result by `course_id` ascending, then by `quarter` ascending (alphabetically: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4).
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE course_completions (course_id VARCHAR(20) PRIMARY KEY, course_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, q1_completions INTEGER, q2_completions INTEGER, q3_completions INTEGER, q4_completions INTEGER);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO course_completions (course_id, course_name, q1_completions, q2_completions, q3_completions, q4_completions) VALUES ('CS101', 'Intro to Python', 45, 52, 48, 61), ('CS102', 'Data Structures', 38, 41, NULL, 44), ('CS103', 'Web Development', 29, 33, 35, 38), ('BUS201', 'Marketing Fundamentals', 51, 48, 46, 50);
test_data: INSERT INTO course_completions (course_id, course_name, q1_completions, q2_completions, q3_completions, q4_completions) VALUES ('AI301', 'Machine Learning', 67, 72, 68, 75), ('AI302', 'Deep Learning', NULL, 45, 48, 51), ('AI303', 'NLP Fundamentals', 33, NULL, 37, 39), ('DATA401', 'Big Data Analytics', 58, 62, 65, 71), ('DATA402', 'Data Visualization', 41, 44, NULL, 49), ('DATA403', 'Statistics', 52, 55, 58, NULL), ('WEB501', 'Frontend Frameworks', 38, 41, 43, 46), ('WEB502', 'Backend APIs', 29, 32, 35, 38), ('WEB503', 'DevOps Essentials', 44, NULL, NULL, 52), ('MOBILE601', 'iOS Development', 25, 28, 30, 33), ('MOBILE602', 'Android Development', 31, 34, 36, 39), ('MOBILE603', 'React Native', NULL, NULL, 22, 25), ('CLOUD701', 'AWS Fundamentals', 63, 67, 70, 74), ('CLOUD702', 'Azure Essentials', 48, 51, 54, 58), ('CLOUD703', 'GCP Basics', 39, 42, 45, 48);

composite_moves: reshape: unpivot 4 wide columns (q1_completions, q2_completions, q3_completions, q4_completions) into long format using UNION ALL of 4 SELECTs, each with literal quarter label; output row count is (input rows) × 4; include NULL values; order by course_id, quarter

hints: PostgreSQL doesn't have a native UNPIVOT command. You'll need to use UNION ALL to stack results from multiple SELECT statements.

Write one SELECT for each quarter column (q1_completions, q2_completions, q3_completions, q4_completions). Each SELECT should return course_id, a literal string for the quarter name ('Q1', 'Q2', etc.), and the corresponding completion count column.

Use UNION ALL to combine: SELECT course_id, 'Q1' AS quarter, q1_completions AS completion_count FROM course_completions UNION ALL SELECT course_id, 'Q2', q2_completions FROM course_completions ... and so on for Q3 and Q4. Order the final result by course_id, then quarter.
answer_key: SELECT course_id, 'Q1' AS quarter, q1_completions AS completion_count FROM course_completions UNION ALL SELECT course_id, 'Q2' AS quarter, q2_completions AS completion_count FROM course_completions UNION ALL SELECT course_id, 'Q3' AS quarter, q3_completions AS completion_count FROM course_completions UNION ALL SELECT course_id, 'Q4' AS quarter, q4_completions AS completion_count FROM course_completions ORDER BY course_id, quarter;

_meta.scenario: an online course platform tracking course completion and certification
